claim: The MBD7 complex suppresses transcriptional silencing of two LUCIFERASE (LUC) reporters via a mechanism that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
source: Here we identified a METHYL-CpG-BINDING DOMAIN 7 (MBD7) complex in Arabidopsis thaliana that suppresses the transcriptional silencing of two LUCIFERASE (LUC) reporters via a mechanism that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on the study's results.

claim: Mutations in components of the MBD7 complex resulted in modest increases in DNA methylation concomitant with decreased LUC expression.
source: Although mutations in components of the MBD7 complex resulted in modest increases in DNA methylation concomitant with decreased LUC expression, we found that these hyper-methylation and gene expression phenotypes can be genetically uncoupled.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study's experimental data.

claim: The hyper-methylation and gene expression phenotypes in MBD7 complex mutants can be genetically uncoupled.
source: Although mutations in components of the MBD7 complex resulted in modest increases in DNA methylation concomitant with decreased LUC expression, we found that these hyper-methylation and gene expression phenotypes can be genetically uncoupled.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on genetic experiments.

claim: Genome-wide profiling experiments showed minimal changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex.
source: This finding, along with genome-wide profiling experiments showing minimal changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex, places the MBD7 complex amongst a small number of factors acting downstream of DNA methylation.
evidence: The abstract states this as a result from genome-wide profiling experiments.

claim: The MBD7 complex is unique as it functions to suppress, rather than enforce, DNA methylation-mediated gene silencing.
source: This complex, however, is unique as it functions to suppress, rather than enforce, DNA methylation-mediated gene silencing.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a distinguishing feature of the MBD7 complex.

claim: In Arabidopsis, methylated regions of the genome can be separated into two main categories: transposons and repeats with heavy methylation in all sequence contexts, and body-methylated genes with CG-only methylation that remain highly expressed.
source: In Arabidopsis, methylated regions of the genome can be separated into two main categories: (1) transposons and repeats that are heavily methylated at cytosines in all sequence contexts (namely CG, CHG and CHH where H indicates A, T or C), leading to gene silencing, and (2) body-methylated genes that harbor methylation exclusively in the CG context but remain highly expressed (Lister et al., 2008; Cokus et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: De novo methylation of cytosines in all sequence contexts requires the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway.
source: De novo methylation of cytosines in all sequence contexts requires the RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) pathway (Law et al., 2010a; Matzke and Mosher, 2014), which utilizes both 24-nucleotide small interfering RNAs (24-nt siRNAs) and long non-coding RNAs to target the de novo methyltransferase, DOMAINS REARRANGED METHYLTRANSFERASE 2 (DRM2), to repetitive regions of the genome.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: Maintenance of CG methylation requires DNA METHYLTRANSFERASE 1 (MET1).
source: Briefly, maintenance of CG methylation requires DNA METHYLTRANSFERASE 1 (MET1), whereas maintenance of CHG methylation (and some CHH methylation) relies on the activity of two related DNA methyltransferases, CHROMOMETHYLASE 2 and 3 (CMT2 and CMT3) (Stroud et al., 2014; Zemach et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: Maintenance of CHG methylation relies on the activity of CHROMOMETHYLASE 2 and 3 (CMT2 and CMT3).
source: Briefly, maintenance of CG methylation requires DNA METHYLTRANSFERASE 1 (MET1), whereas maintenance of CHG methylation (and some CHH methylation) relies on the activity of two related DNA methyltransferases, CHROMOMETHYLASE 2 and 3 (CMT2 and CMT3) (Stroud et al., 2014; Zemach et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: The remaining CHH methylation is maintained by DRM2 via the continuous action of the RdDM pathway.
source: Finally, the remaining CHH methylation is maintained by DRM2 via the continuous action of the RdDM pathway.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the context of DNA methylation maintenance pathways.

claim: ROS1, DML2, and DML3 act in a semi-redundant manner to remove DNA methylation in vegetative tissue.
source: While DME plays an essential role during plant reproduction, ROS1, DML2, and DML3 act in a semi-redundant manner to remove DNA methylation in vegetative tissue (Lister et al., 2008; Zhu, 2009; Penterman et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: In ros1 dml2 dml3 (rdd) triple mutants, a subset of genes are silenced.
source: These proteins tend to remove DNA methylation in regions that flank genes, and in ros1 dml2 dml3 (rdd) triple mutants a subset of these genes are silenced, leading to a model in which ROS1, DML2 and DML3 function to remove DNA methylation and prevent transcriptional gene silencing (Lister et al., 2008; Zhu, 2009; Penterman et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: In Arabidopsis, there are 13 proteins that contain MBD domains (MBD1-13).
source: In Arabidopsis, there are 13 proteins that contain MBD domains (MBD1-13) (Grafi et al., 2007; Zemach and Grafi, 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 bind methylated DNA in vitro and localize to highly methylated, peri-centromeric regions of the genome in vivo.
source: Of these MBD proteins, early studies demonstrated that MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 bind methylated DNA in vitro and localize to highly methylated, peri-centromeric regions of the genome in vivo, suggesting roles for these factors in gene silencing (Zemach and Grafi, 2003; Scebba et al., 2003; Ito et al., 2003; Zemach et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: MBD6 and MBD10 play roles in nucleolar dominance and rDNA silencing.
source: For example, MBD6 and MBD10 play roles in nucleolar dominance and rDNA silencing (Preuss et al., 2008), whereas MBD7 has been implicated in DNA demethylation based on genetic connections with the DNA demethylase, ROS1 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claim: MBD7 has been implicated in DNA demethylation based on genetic connections with the DNA demethylase, ROS1.
source: For example, MBD6 and MBD10 play roles in nucleolar dominance and rDNA silencing (Preuss et al., 2008), whereas MBD7 has been implicated in DNA demethylation based on genetic connections with the DNA demethylase, ROS1 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: MORPHEUS MOLECULE 1 (MOM1) is required for the silencing of methylated loci but does not control the levels of DNA methylation.
source: Previous genetic screens have identified MORPHEUS MOLECULE 1 (MOM1) (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012), and MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012; Brabbs et al., 2013), as genes that are required for the silencing of methylated loci but that do not control the levels of DNA methylation (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012; Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) are required for the silencing of methylated loci but do not control the levels of DNA methylation.
source: Previous genetic screens have identified MORPHEUS MOLECULE 1 (MOM1) (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012), and MICRORCHIDIA 1 and 6 (MORC1 and MORC6) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012; Brabbs et al., 2013), as genes that are required for the silencing of methylated loci but that do not control the levels of DNA methylation (Amedeo et al., 2000; Won et al., 2012; Moissiard et al., 2012; Lorković et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: Mutations in ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN 5 and 6 (atxr5 and atxr6) release gene silencing without significantly altering the pattern of DNA methylation.
source: In addition, mutations in ARABIDOPSIS TRITHORAX-RELATED PROTEIN 5 and 6 (atxr5 and atxr6) (Jacob et al., 2009) were also found to release gene silencing without significantly altering the pattern of DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claim: SU(VAR)3–9 HOMOLOG 1 (SUVH1) acts downstream of DNA methylation to enable the transcription of methylated loci.
source: On the other hand, only one factor, SU(VAR)3–9 HOMOLOG 1 (SUVH1) (Li et al., 2016), has been identified to act downstream of DNA methylation to enable the transcription of methylated loci.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to a prior study.

claim: The YJ and LUCH reporters differ in their basal levels of LUC expression despite harboring nearly identical transgenes.
source: Here we compared the expression patterns and epigenetic features of the two LUC reporters, which differ in their basal levels of LUC expression despite harboring nearly identical transgenes that contain LUC genes driven by dual cauliflower mosaic virus 35S promoters (d35S) (Figure 1—source data 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study's characterization of the reporters.

claim: At the d35S promoters, the YJ and LUCH transgenes had similar patterns of 24-nt siRNAs and similar levels of DNA methylation in all sequence contexts.
source: At the d35S promoters, the two transgenes had similar patterns of 24-nt siRNAs and similar levels of DNA methylation in all sequence contexts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequencing data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: In LUCH, DNA methylation extended beyond the d35S promoters into the LUC and NPTII coding regions.
source: However, in LUCH, DNA methylation extended beyond the d35S promoters into the LUC and NPTII coding regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequencing data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Analysis of the MethylC-seq data supports the conclusion that the YJ and LUCH reporters represent single and multi-copy insertions into a single genomic locus, respectively.
source: Although both reporters segregate as single-copy insertions, analysis of the MethylC-seq data supports the conclusion that the YJ and LUCH reporters represent single and multi-copy insertions into a single genomic locus, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from analysis of MethylC-seq data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Both YJ and LUCH reporters contain genes that harbor high levels of promoter methylation but are not fully silenced.
source: Despite these differences, both reporters share a common feature that distinguishes them from most endogenous methylated loci: they contain genes that harbor high levels of promoter methylation but are not fully silenced.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study's characterization of the reporters.

claim: Two mutants with reduced luciferase luminescence were identified from independent genetic screens using the YJ and LUCH reporter lines.
source: Two mutants with reduced luciferase luminescence, one in each reporter background, were identified (Figure 1A) and RT-qPCR analysis confirmed reduced LUC expression in these mutant backgrounds relative to their respective controls (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from genetic screens with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The same gene (At1g20870) was disrupted in both lil-1 and lil-2 mutants.
source: Map-based cloning and candidate gene sequencing revealed that the same gene (At1g20870) was disrupted in both mutants.
evidence: This is stated as a result from map-based cloning and sequencing.

claim: The lil-1 allele contains a G-to-A mutation that disrupts the single splice acceptor site of At1g20870.
source: The lil-1 allele contains a G-to-A mutation, which disrupts the single splice acceptor site of At1g20870 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a result from sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The lil-2 allele contains a C-to-T mutation that introduces a premature stop codon.
source: Although lil-2 was isolated from a T-DNA mutagenesis screen, this allele does not contain a T-DNA insertion, but instead contains a C-to-T mutation that introduces a premature stop codon (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a result from sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: LIL is predicted to encode a 51.9 kDa protein containing a carboxy-terminal Alpha Crystallin Domain (ACD) or Heat Shock Protein 20 like (HSP20-like) chaperone domain.
source: LIL is predicted to encode a 51.9 kDa protein containing a carboxy-terminal Alpha Crystallin Domain (ACD) or Heat Shock Protein 20 like (HSP20-like) chaperone domain (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from protein sequence analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: LIL and three paralogs form one clade among the 25 Arabidopsis ACD-containing proteins.
source: Among the 25 Arabidopsis ACD-containing proteins, LIL and three paralogs form one clade (Scharf et al., 2001) (alignments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as a result from phylogenetic analysis with data shown in the referenced figure and citation to prior work.

claim: LIL (also known as INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 3 (IDM3) or INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 2-LIKE 1 (IDL1)) and ROS5/IDM2 were found to prevent DNA hyper-methylation and enable gene expression at other reporter transgenes and select genomic loci.
source: Two members of this clade, LIL (also known as INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 3 (IDM3) [Lang et al., 2015] or INCREASED DNA METHYLATION 2-LIKE 1 (IDL1) [Li et al., 2015b]) and ROS5 (Zhao et al., 2014)/IDM2 (Qian et al., 2014) (At1g54840) were recently found to prevent DNA hyper-methylation and enable gene expression at other reporter transgenes and select genomic loci, demonstrating they also act to suppress gene silencing (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Zhao et al., 2014; Qian et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: LIL interacts with three MBD proteins: MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 in yeast two-hybrid assays.
source: Using full-length LIL as bait and an Arabidopsis cDNA library as prey, LIL was found to interact with three MBD proteins: MBD5, MBD6 and MBD7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from yeast two-hybrid experiments with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: An interaction was detected between the last MBD domain of MBD7 (MBD7d3) and the full length LIL protein.
source: However, an interaction was detected between the last MBD domain of MBD7 (MBD7d3) and the full length LIL protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from yeast two-hybrid experiments with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: A 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD5 co-purifies with ACD15.5 and ACD21.4 as well as low amounts of MBD6.
source: Specifically, a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD5 (pMBD5::MBD5-3x-Flag) was shown to co-purify with ACD15.5 (At1g76440) and ACD21.4 (At1g54850) as well as low amounts of MBD6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Purification of a 3x-HA tagged version of MBD7 revealed a specific interaction with LIL.
source: while purification of a 3x-HA tagged version of MBD7 (pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA) revealed a specific interaction with LIL (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Purification of a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD7 yielded peptides corresponding to LIL, ROS4, ROS5, HDP1, and HDP2.
source: As MBD7 had previously been shown to also associate with ROS4, ROS5 (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), and HARBINGER TRANSPOSON-DERIVED PROTEIN 1 (HDP1) and HDP2 (Duan et al., 2017), additional purifications using a 3x-Flag-tagged version of MBD7 (pMBD7::MBD7-3xFlag) were conducted and these experiments yielded peptides corresponding to LIL as well as all the aforementioned MBD7-associated proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a result from affinity purification and mass spectrometry with data shown in the referenced figure and citations to prior work.

claim: MBD5 and MBD7 associate with different subsets of ACD proteins to form distinct MBD-ACD protein complexes.
source: Taken together, these findings demonstrate that MBD5 and MBD7 associate with different subsets of ACD proteins to form distinct MBD-ACD protein complexes, the roles and compositions of which are just beginning to be explored.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the affinity purification and mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: The mbd5 mutations had no effect on LUC expression at the YJ reporter.
source: The mbd5 mutations had no effect on LUC expression at the YJ reporter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: In the mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants, LUC expression was reduced to similar levels as observed in lil-1.
source: Conversely, in the mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants, LUC expression was reduced to similar levels as observed in lil-1 (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Expression of the d35S-driven NPTII gene present in both YJ and LUCH reporters was reduced in mbd7, ros4, ros5, and lil mutants.
source: In addition, expression of the d35S-driven NPTII gene present in both YJ and LUCH reporters was also reduced in these mutants (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a result from expression analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Treatment with 5-Aza-dC results in increased LUC expression in both YJ and LUCH reporters.
source: Previous analyses have shown that both the YJ (Li et al., 2016) and LUCH (Won et al., 2012) reporters are regulated by DNA methylation such that treatment with the cytosine methylation inhibitor 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine (5-Aza-dC) results in increased LUC expression.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: The levels of LUC expression in lil and mbd7 mutants treated with 5-Aza-dC were indistinguishable from their respective controls.
source: To determine if DNA methylation is necessary for the phenotypes observed upon disruption of the MBD7 complex, we assessed the effects of 5-Aza-dC treatment on LUC expression in several alleles of lil and mbd7 and found the levels of LUC expression in these mutants were indistinguishable from their respective controls (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from 5-Aza-dC treatment experiments with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: LIL and MBD7 are only necessary for the expression of the LUC reporters when they harbor DNA methylation.
source: Thus, LIL and MBD7 are only necessary for the expression of the LUC reporters when they harbor DNA methylation, affirming their roles in the transcriptional, rather than post-transcriptional, regulation of LUC expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the 5-Aza-dC treatment experiments.

claim: Amplification of the d35S promoter was reduced in both lil mutants relative to their respective controls in McrBC restriction enzyme assays, indicating increased DNA methylation.
source: Using this assay, amplification of the d35S promoter was reduced in both lil mutants relative to their respective controls, indicating that mutations in LIL increased the level of DNA methylation at the d35S promoter (Figure 4A; gel based).
evidence: This is stated as a result from McrBC restriction enzyme assays with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Similar results were obtained for lil-1, mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants when qPCR was performed to quantify DNA levels from mock or McrBC treated samples.
source: Similar results were obtained for lil-1, mbd7, ros4, and ros5 mutants when qPCR was performed to quantify DNA levels from mock or McrBC treated samples (Figure 4B; qPCR).
evidence: This is stated as a result from McrBC-qPCR assays with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Quantification of the average methylation levels across the d35S promoter revealed a modest but consistent increase in DNA methylation in the CG context in lil-2, mbd7-5, and three biological replicates of lil-1.
source: At the LUC reporters, quantification of the average methylation levels across the d35S promoter (282–1036 nt) revealed a surprisingly modest but consistent increase in DNA methylation in the CG context in lil-2, mbd7-5, and three biological replicates of lil-1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The hyper-methylation in lil and mbd7 mutants is largely restricted to a small region at the 3' end of the d35S promoter.
source: Further inspection of the DNA methylation profiles revealed that this hyper-methylation is largely restricted to a small region at the 3' end of the d35S promoter, which is within the region amplified in the McrBC-PCR methyl-cutting assays (Figure 4C; right panels).
evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: In the lil-2 mutant, a slight increase in CG and CHG methylation, but no change in CHH methylation, was observed at the LUCH reporter.
source: In the lil-2 mutant, a slight increase in CG and CHG methylation, but no change in CHH methylation, was observed at the LUCH reporter (Figure 4D; Full McrBC).
evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: For the lil-1 replicates and mbd7-5, a more prominent increase in CG and CHG methylation was observed.
source: For the lil-1 replicates and mbd7-5, a more prominent increase in CG and CHG methylation was observed, and these DNA methylation defects were significantly reversed by introduction of an MBD7-3xHA construct that rescues the LUC expression phenotype at the YJ reporter (Figure 4D short McrBC and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, respectively).
evidence: This is stated as a result from MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Enrichment was observed at the d35S promoter using a MBD7-GFP line driven by a 35S promoter in ChIP experiments.
source: While no enrichment was observed with either the 3xHA or 3xFlag tagged MBD7 proteins expressed under their native promoters, enrichment was observed at the d35S promoter using a previously characterized MBD7-GFP line driven by a 35S promoter (Wang et al., 2015) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated as a result from ChIP experiments with data shown in the referenced figure and citation to prior work.

claim: The DNA methylation levels observed at the 35S promoter by traditional bisulfite sequencing show similar patterns of methylation in the lil and mbd7 mutants when compared to the MethylC-seq data.
source: The DNA methylation levels observed at the 35S promoter by traditional bisulfite sequencing are represented in browser track format (Figure 5A and Supplementary file 1D: YJ_tradBS_WigTracks) and show similar patterns of methylation in the lil and mbd7 mutants when compared to the MethylC-seq data (Figure 4C,D), in that hyper-methylation (primarily in the CG and CHG contexts) was detected at the 3' end of the promoter (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The increased methylation observed in the mbd7-5 mutant was restored to a more wild-type level upon introduction of the pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA transgene.
source: Also consistent with the MethylC-seq data, the increased methylation observed in the mbd7-5 mutant was restored to a more wild-type level upon introduction of the pMBD7::MBD7-3xHA transgene (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The traditional bisulfite sequencing revealed a uniform distribution of methylation at the YJ reporter.
source: These analyses revealed a uniform distribution of methylation at the YJ reporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Decreases in non-CG methylation were observed in the ago4-6 and nrpe1-11 mutants predominantly at regions of the promoter producing large amounts of 24-nt siRNAs.
source: At the level of DNA methylation, decreases in non-CG methylation were observed in the ago4-6 and nrpe1-11 mutants predominantly at regions of the promoter producing large amounts of 24-nt siRNAs, as predicted for components of the RNA-directed DNA methylation pathway (Figure 5A; '24-nt siRNA clusters').
evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: All three mutants (ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd) showed a hyper-methylation phenotype similar to that observed in the lil and mbd7 mutants at the 3' end of the 35S promoter.
source: Conversely, all three mutants (ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd) showed a hyper-methylation phenotype similar to that observed in the lil and mbd7 mutants at the 3' end of the 35S promoter (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from traditional bisulfite sequencing with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Although the ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd mutants exhibit similar hyper-methylation phenotypes in the CG and CHG contexts at the 3' end of the 35S promoter, LUC expression is much higher in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants than in the rdd mutant.
source: Notably, although the ago4-6, nrpe1-11 and rdd mutants exhibit similar hyper-methylation phenotypes in the CG and CHG contexts at the 3' end of the 35S promoter, LUC expression is much higher in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants than in the rdd mutant (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is stated as a result from expression and methylation analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter region alone is not sufficient to cause gene silencing at the YJ reporter.
source: While compensatory effects on gene expression due to decreased non-CG methylation at other regions of the d35S promoter in the ago4 and nrpe1 mutants cannot be fully excluded, these findings suggest that the hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter region alone is not sufficient to cause gene silencing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analysis of ago4, nrpe1, and rdd mutants.

claim: At the YJ reporter, the MBD7 complex can regulate gene expression in a manner that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
source: Taken together, these analyses reveal that at the YJ reporter the MBD7 complex can regulate gene expression in a manner that is largely downstream of DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the genetic uncoupling experiments.

claim: Thousands of DMRs were identified in each of the lil-1 and mbd7 datasets, mostly in the CG and CHH contexts.
source: Although thousands of DMRs were identified in each of the lil-1 and mbd7 datasets, mostly in the CG and CHH contexts (Supplementary file 2A), the vast majority of these DMRs were not in common between the different alleles or even between biological replicates (Supplementary file 2B-F, see orange highlighted comparisons).
evidence: This is stated as a result from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis.

claim: When the DMRs from the three lil-1 replicates were compared with the DMRs identified in lil-2, mbd7-3 and mbd7-4, only 33 hyper and one hypo DMRs remained.
source: Indeed, when the DMRs from the three lil-1 replicates were compared with the DMRs identified in lil-2, mbd7-3 and mbd7-4, only 33 hyper and one hypo DMRs remained (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 2F; 6-way DMR overlaps, and Supplementary file 2G-J), and these regions converged on 20 loci (19 displayed hyper-methylation and one showed hypo-methylation [Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1]).
evidence: This is stated as a result from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Very few genomic targets show consistent changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex.
source: Thus, while numerous DMRs can be identified between any single mbd7 or lil mutant vs. control (Supplementary file 2A), very few genomic targets show consistent changes in DNA methylation upon disruption of the MBD7 complex, indicating that these changes may represent natural variation in methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from genome-wide MethylC-seq analysis.

claim: A relaxed set of DMRs yielded 194 CG hyper DMRs, 310 CHG hyper DMRs and 52 CHH hyper DMRs.
source: This yielded a set of 194 CG hyper DMRs, 310 CHG hyper DMRs and 52 CHH hyper DMRs (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from relaxed DMR analysis with data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Only a third of the hyper mC DMRs in mbd7 and lil mutants overlap with regions hyper-methylated in the rdd mutant background.
source: Notably, only a third of these regions overlap with regions hyper-methylated in the rdd mutant background, representing a tiny fraction of the total rdd targets (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated as a result from comparison of DMRs with data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The demethylation pathway does not appear to function in a manner that depends solely on either MBD7 or LIL.
source: Thus, although there are clear genetic connections between MBD7, LIL and ROS1 in the regulation of several transgenic reporters (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), as a general rule, the demethylation pathway does not appear to function in a manner that depends solely on either MBD7 or LIL.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the DMR overlap analysis with citations to prior work.

claim: Re-introduction of LIL is not able to efficiently correct the observed hyper-methylation defects.
source: These findings demonstrate that re-introduction of LIL is not able to efficiently correct the observed hyper-methylation defects, which further supports the notion that these changes represent variation in methylation rather than a direct effect of the lil mutation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from complementation experiments.

claim: No overlapping mis-regulated genes were identified between the lil and mbd7 alleles in transcriptome profiling.
source: Among these mutants, no overlapping mis-regulated genes were identified between the lil and mbd7 alleles (Supplementary file 3)
evidence: This is stated as a result from transcriptome profiling.

claim: Only one of the genes previously identified as a target of MBD7 complex was consistently down-regulated in any of the mutants tested.
source: and only one of the genes previously identified as a target of MBD7 complex (i.e. down-regulated genes associated with hyper DMRs in the Columbia ecotype (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Qian et al., 2014; Duan et al., 2017; Qian et al., 2012)) was consistently down-regulated in any of the mutants tested (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result from transcriptome profiling with data shown in the referenced figure and citations to prior work.

claim: The MBD7 complex likely functions redundantly with other MBD-ACD complexes and/or is required only under specific conditions.
source: Given the absence of detectable endogenous targets transcriptionally regulated by the MBD7 complex, it is likely that this complex functions redundantly with other MBD-ACD complexes and/or is required only under specific conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the absence of endogenous targets.

claim: Loss of the MBD7-LIL complex results in the silencing of LUC reporter constructs with minimal changes in DNA methylation.
source: Nonetheless, our findings demonstrate that this complex has the ability to regulate gene expression in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation at LUC reporters. Firstly, we found that loss of the MBD7-LIL complex results in the silencing of these reporter constructs with minimal changes in DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter in the YJ reporter does not appear to be sufficient to cause gene silencing.
source: Secondly, we demonstrated that hyper-methylation at the 3' end of the d35S promoter in the YJ reporter does not appear to be sufficient to cause gene silencing (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the study's findings with reference to data shown in the figure.

claim: MBD7 and LIL represent the first anti-silencing complex placed downstream of DNA methylation.
source: However, unlike these other downstream effectors, which function to reinforce gene silencing, MBD7 and LIL represent the first anti-silencing complex placed downstream of DNA methylation, functioning to enable gene expression despite high levels of promoter DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion comparing the MBD7 complex to other known downstream effectors.

claim: The MBD7 complex may function in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation rather than as part of the DNA demethylation pathway.
source: Rather than functioning as part of the DNA demethylation pathway, as has been previously hypothesized (Lang et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al., 2015), our results suggest that the MBD7 complex may function in a manner largely downstream of DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings with citations to prior hypotheses.

claim: The two ACD domain-containing proteins (LIL/IDL1/IDM3 and ROS5/IDM2) interact directly with each other.

claim: Loss of MORC1, MORC6, ATXR5 and ATXR6 results in de-compaction of peri-centromeric heterochromatin and the selective up-regulation of genes and transposons located within these regions.
source: Many of these factors, including MORC1, MORC6, ATXR5 and ATXR6, influence chromatin organization on a gross scale, such that loss of these factors results in de-compaction of peri-centromeric heterochromatin (i.e., chromocenters) (Moissiard et al., 2012; Jacob et al., 2009) and the selective up-regulation of genes and transposons located within these regions (Moissiard et al., 2012; Jacob et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior studies.

claim: MOM1 appears to act on a finer scale to influence gene expression without significantly perturbing chromatin compaction.

claim: In mbd7 and lil mutants, no obvious defects in chromocenter formation were observed.
source: In mbd7 and lil mutants, no obvious defects in chromocenter formation were observed, suggesting the MBD7 complex may act at a local level to enable the expression of methylated genes, perhaps antagonizing the function of MOM1, which has been shown to regulate expression at the LUCH reporter (Won et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study with a citation to prior work.

source: However, the MBD7d3 construct used here represents an extended version of the third MBD domain that has minimal overlap with the StkC domain, suggesting that the interaction between MBD7 and LIL can be mediated by several regions of the MBD7 protein, namely, the StkC domain (Lang et al., 2015), as well as the last MBD domain (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
